overview: Genomic DNA is the organism's natural DNA including introns; cDNA is lab-made DNA synthesised from mRNA, so it lacks introns.
genZNote: Genomic DNA is the unedited manuscript with all the footnotes (introns). cDNA is the cleaned-up, footnote-free final draft.

aspects.label: Contains Introns?
aspects.valueA: Yes — includes both exons and introns, plus regulatory regions.
aspects.valueB: No — introns are already removed since it's made from mature, spliced mRNA.

aspects.label: How It's Obtained
aspects.valueA: Extracted directly from a cell's nucleus.
aspects.valueB: Synthesised in the lab from mRNA using the enzyme reverse transcriptase.

aspects.label: Typical Use
aspects.valueA: Whole-genome sequencing, studying gene structure and regulatory regions.
aspects.valueB: Gene cloning for expression in bacteria (which can't splice introns), building expression libraries.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: cDNA is essential for expressing eukaryotic genes in bacteria, since bacteria have no splicing machinery to remove introns.
overlay.memoryTrick: cDNA = 'clean' DNA copy of mRNA, no introns.
overlay.commonMisconception: cDNA is not simply 'DNA from the cytoplasm' — the 'c' stands for complementary, referring to its synthesis from an RNA template.
